title: fix(runtime): AppPlugin's job scheduling and datasource readers take the boot's converted copy
body:
Fixes #23029
Clause-②: no

## What changes

`AppPlugin` now hands job scheduling and the datasource readers the boot's ONE ADR-0087 forward conversion (`forwardConverted`, #22994). That is the copy `manifest.register` and the security registrar already take. Every reader takes the memoized result, so there is no second conversion pass.

| reader (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`) | before (`origin/main` 7f2f081e8a) | after |
|---|---|---|
| job scheduling: `collectBundleJobs` guard + `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` on `kernel:ready` | `this.bundle` (raw) | `this.forwardConverted(ctx).definition` |
| code-defined datasource registration (`registerInMemory` + `applyProtection`) and its owner walk (`codeDefinedDatasourceOwners`) | `this.collections.datasources`; `packages[]` bodies walked raw | `convertedCollection(ctx, 'datasources')`; `packages[]` bodies walked on the converted copy |
| reserved-name check (`default`) | `this.collections.datasources` | `convertedCollection(ctx, 'datasources')` |
| `connectDeclared` input (`datasources`, `objects`) | `this.collections.datasources` / `.objects` | `convertedCollection(ctx, 'datasources' / 'objects')` |

`convertedCollection` is a new private accessor. The converted copy is `{ ...manifest, ...collections }`, so where the stack declares no `datasources` / `objects` it would carry the manifest's keys of that name. Those are the glob-pattern lists `ManifestSchema` declares, and these readers have never read them. So which SOURCE a collection comes from is decided on the raw collections, the rule the security block already uses for #18034. The VALUE comes from the converted copy. For jobs, `collectBundleJobs`' "stack `jobs`, else legacy `manifest.jobs`" rule gives the same answer on the converted copy, because the stack wins the spread. The legacy `manifest.jobs` list is now converted too.

Untouched: `loadTranslations`, `bindAppArtifactHandlers`, `datasourceMapping`, `init()`, and `forwardConverted` itself.

## Premise, measured before the change

**Registry entries.** All three exist. They live in `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts` (`ALL_CONVERSIONS`, which `applyArtifactForwardConversions` in `packages/metadata-core` replays). Each is `toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.3.0'`:
- `job-timeout-to-timeout-ms` (registry order 22): `jobs[].timeout` becomes `timeoutMs`.
- `turso-config-timeout-to-timeout-ms` (order 28): turso `config.timeout` becomes `config.timeoutMs`.
- `memory-persistence-auto-save-interval-to-ms` (order 27): memory `config.persistence.autoSaveInterval` becomes `autoSaveIntervalMs`.

**Reach**, on `origin/main` 7f2f081e8a. The bundle is a `plugins[]` entry, wrapped by `materializeStackPlugin` into `new AppPlugin(bundle)`, the rule `os serve` and `os migrate` mount it by. It is booted with init, start and `kernel:ready`:
- **No `engines.protocol`.** The D1 handshake admits it with one warn, and the window is `converted-undeclared`. Results:
  - The job was scheduled with NO options (`timeoutMs` absent, so the adapter default applies).
  - `edge_db` was registered and handed to `connectDeclared` as `config: { url, timeout: 30000 }`.
  - `local_cache` was registered and handed over with `persistence.autoSaveInterval: 5000`.
- **`engines.protocol: '>=17.0.0'`.** The same three drops, with no warn at all.
- **`engines.protocol: '^17.0.0'`.** Refused at D1 (`ProtocolIncompatibleError`, the runtime is protocol 18.0.0) before any reader runs. Loud, so it is not this defect.
- **A `packages[]` bundle whose BODY carries `jobs[].timeout`.** Refused loudly by the entry parse (`resolveArtifactPackageOrder`: "`packages[0]` is not a package entry … `manifest.jobs.0.timeout`: `job.timeout` was removed"), before any reader runs. So on that shape the readers never see the keys, before or after this change. A `packages[]` bundle that arrives through `loadArtifactBundle` has its bodies converted at load (#23027).

## `loadTranslations`, measured and NOT changed

It reads raw `this.collections.translations`. The bundle carried all three major-18 translation retirements under `zh-CN`:
- `settings` (`translation-per-app-settings-removed`, retiredAfter 17.4.0);
- `pages.home.components.f1.submitLabel` (`translation-component-submit-label-removed`, 17.2.0);
- `dashboards.pulse.widgets.w1.subCaption` (`translation-widget-sub-caption-removed`, 17.6.0).

The bundle was booted through `AppPlugin.start`, and `getTranslations('zh-CN')` was read. That is the answer `GET /api/v1/i18n/translations/:locale` serves.
- **The in-memory fallback and `FileI18nAdapter` alike** serve all three retired keys.
- **The converted copy** strips all three, with three notices.

So the raw read does change what the i18n service serves. Per the entries' own summaries, `settings` is the one with an effect: a per-app `settings` group still fills gaps in the merged tree. The other two are served and read by nothing. This is reported only; the card rules it out of this change.

## Tests

`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin-converted-readers.test.ts` has 6 tests. Each boots the bundle through the same `plugins[]` route:
- **The job.** `jobs[].timeout: 40` on a `while (true) {}` body is scheduled with `{ retryPolicy: undefined, timeoutMs: 40 }`, and its run rejects with "exceeded CPU budget of 40ms".
- **The turso datasource.** It is registered `toStrictEqual` its converted shape plus the unchanged `origin` / `_packageId` / `_packageVersion` / `_provenance` stamps, and handed to `connectDeclared` with `config.timeoutMs`.
- **The memory datasource.** The same, with `persistence.autoSaveIntervalMs`.
- **One conversion.** `connectDeclared` is handed the very `datasources` and `objects` arrays the `manifest` service registered (identity).
- **CONTROL, current spellings.**
  - The job keeps `timeoutMs`.
  - Every datasource is registered byte for byte as `{ ...authored, ...stamps }`.
  - `connectDeclared` receives the authored arrays BY REFERENCE (copy-on-write).
  - The authored object is not stamped.
- **CONTROL, manifest globs.** A manifest carrying `datasources` / `objects` glob lists, with a stack that declares neither, registers and connects nothing.

**Ablation** ran inside `os-verify-lock`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (WRAP mode) plus a restore trap, on committed `372ea7faf3`. `app-plugin.ts` reaches the suite by relative source import, so no rebuild is involved. Each leg landed (anchor 1 to 0, blob `653250ea2154` changed), and each restore was proven (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty):
- **A, the job reader back to `this.bundle`.** Exactly the job pin went red: "expected undefined to deeply equal { retryPolicy: undefined, … }". 5 passed.
- **B, `convertedCollection` reading raw.** The turso, memory and one-conversion pins went red (the diff shows `timeoutMs` against `timeout`). 3 passed, both controls included.
- **C, the raw-source guard deleted.** Exactly the manifest-globs control went red: `connectDeclared` was handed `datasources: ['src/**/*.datasource.ts']`.

## Verification, all at `9c1768d541`

`9c1768d541` is this branch merged with `origin/main` `0aef788816`.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test`**, run as `exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: Test Files 361 passed (361), Tests 5162 passed, 19 skipped. The `--project repo` layer: 3 passed (3), 751 tests.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`:** exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` reports "OK … 27 file(s) / 190 error(s) / 68 pinned signature(s) held". `tsc --listFiles -p tsconfig.test.json` compiles the new test, with 0 errors in it.
- **The #22994 / #22989 pins, and the job and datasource neighbours,** run verbose:
  - #22994 / #22989 pins: `app-plugin-converted-collections`, `standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy`, `app-plugin-config-door-api-items`, `app-plugin-api-matcher-absent-warning`;
  - neighbours: `app-plugin.datasource-provenance`, `app-plugin.jobs`, `app-plugin.option-b-packages`, `app-plugin.job-data-reach`, `app-plugin-artifact-forward-conversion`, `app-plugin.manifest-security-collision`;
  - result: 11 files, 81 tests, all green.
- **Gates.** `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derives 63, with the claim's paths and with none alike. All 63 exit 0.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3). After `turbo run build` (73/73) it passed: "107 published require entry point(s) across 66 package(s) load".
  - `--ran` reconciliation: "63 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero …)".
- **Lint, narrowed to the touched files, with three proofs.**
  - `--print-config` puts both `.ts` files in eslint's population, with 6 and 5 rules. The changeset `.md` is outside it.
  - `--format json` reports 3 files: 2 linted with 0 errors and 0 warnings, and the `.md` "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied".
  - Every `parserOptions` in `eslint.config.mjs` is `{ ecmaVersion, sourceType }`, so no type-aware linting is on. The rules are AST selectors, and the baseline JSON files the config reads are untouched. So no untouched file's verdict can move.

## Acceptance notes

- **A handler job's `ctx.bundle`** is now the converted copy. For a nested-manifest bundle that is `{ ...manifest, ...collections }`, the payload `manifest.register` gets. For a flat bundle that converts nothing, it is the same reference as before. `JobHandlerContext.bundle` documents "declarations, not a data handle", and no in-tree production handler reads it (the option-B pin that does stays green).
- **Record-spelled `datasources`** (`{ edge_db: { … } }`) are not converted by the conversion layer. `mapDatasources` walks arrays only. Measured: `applyArtifactForwardConversions` over a record-spelled turso `config.timeout` gives 0 notices and leaves the key unconverted. `AppPlugin`'s readers accept that spelling. `defineStack` normalizes maps to arrays and `os build` emits arrays, so no producer is named. Carrier: none.
- **`datasourceMapping`** is still read raw. No registry entry walks it today.
- **Same family, outside this card's surface:** `bindAppArtifactHandlers(ql, this.bundle, …)` binds hooks from the RAW bundle. Measured through the same route: a hook authored with the retired `timeout: 5000` (`hook-timeout-to-timeout-ms`, retiredAfter 17.3.0) reaches `ql.bindHooks` as `{ timeout: 5000 }` with no `timeoutMs`. The wrapper reads only `meta.timeoutMs` (`packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts`). Reported to the seat; not fixed here.
